name: PT Mitrabara Adiperdana Tbk

frontmatter.title: Mitrabara Adiperdana — a cash-backed coal run-off corrected to the last actual
frontmatter.summary: MBAP is a North Kalimantan thermal-coal producer whose Malinau reserve runs out in 2028. The equity is mostly net cash plus a small non-coal platform; the coal business is a short annuity. We correct the value to the last actual: the balance sheet is rolled to the DCF date and the observed 2026 realisation is held, not haircut. We move to ADD with a target of Rp1,962, while flagging the name as not actionable at its traded value.
thesis: The reserve is the clock. Malinau holds 3.00 Mt in-ground at May 2026; the company plans to sell 1.45 Mt in 2026 and produce 1.30 Mt a year in 2027-28, and says the mine ends in 2028 [S9][S10]. We model the run-off and assume no replacement mine in the base; [S10] is a free option, not a forecast.

The balance sheet is the value floor. Net cash of US$113.4m less US$40.0m of debt at 30 June, restricted cash and a non-coal platform carried at its sunk-capex floor cover most of the market capitalisation before any coal cash flow [S4][S5].

The 2026 actual is price, not volume. Nine-month revenue of US$151.1m against flat cost of revenues of US$106.0m gives gross profit of US$45.1m [S12]. Holding the observed 9M2026 realisation of 0.87 through the forecast, rather than cutting it in the two years that carry the coal value, is the main correction to the previous cautious base.

The strongest case against us is capital allocation and liquidity, not geology. The US$105.0m 2026 capex programme is almost the market capitalisation and 97.0% of it is for subsidiaries with no disclosed return target [S9]. The free float is 9.7% and the shares trade IDR252.7m a day; the engine flags the name non-investable on ADTV.

The peer-median EV/EBITDA cross-check carries only 15% of the blend because the engine's metric is the FY2025A trough; on a short reserve life a single-year multiple assumes a going concern the DCF does not. The life DCF carries the target.

catalysts.event: 2027 RKAB approval and FY2026 coal production/sales disclosure
Wood-pellet plant targeted for commercial operation
FY2026 audited results, annual report and any reserve statement
Annual general meeting, FY2026 dividend decision and board changes
Malinau reserve exhausted, mine closure and reclamation

blocks.text: We rate MBAP **ADD** with a target of Rp1,962, a total return of 12.5% against the Rp1,745 price. The target is Rp2,453 before the 20% house liquidity discount. The primary method is the life-of-asset DCF at Rp2,117; the peer EV/EBITDA cross-check at Rp2,371 carries the remaining weight.

This revision answers the round-one review by correcting two things that made the base cautious rather than most likely. First, the DCF is dated 30 September 2026 but the bridge used the 30 June balance; we roll the balance sheet to the DCF date so the quarter that earned US$17.0m of nine-month profit is not lost. Second, the realisation was cut from 0.87 to a trough-market ratio in FY2027E-FY2028E with no source; we hold the observed 2026 ratio. Both changes raise value. We also remove an unsourced impairment of the capex programme from the base and move the cash-deployment stress into the bear case, where it belongs.

At the current price the market capitalisation is IDR2,141,589.6m. Net cash is a large share of that, so the equity is a leveraged call on the short coal annuity plus whatever the non-coal platform becomes. The reverse DCF says the price implies a Newcastle marker above the deck's forward path but below spot; the price is not obviously wrong, but the corrected model says it is too low.

The rating is mechanical. The engine's investable flag is false because three-month ADTV is IDR252.7m, below the house threshold, and the 20% liquidity discount alone is the difference between the pre-discount target and a modest total return. A comparable name, IATA, was passed on the same test. We maintain coverage and the valuation, but **ADD is not an actionable position at this traded value**; the Sector Lead should sign off with that limitation explicit.

MBAP mines thermal coal at Malinau, North Kalimantan, under an IUP for production operations held since 2009 [S3]. The product is a 5,400 kcal/kg GAR kcal/kg GAR coal sold on the export market and into the domestic obligation; the consolidated group also owns mining-services, solar, wood-pellet and shrimp businesses that contributed 17.6% of FY2025 revenue [S3][S9].

The controlling shareholder is PT Wahana Sentosa Cemerlang with 60.0% [S3]. The public free float is 9.7% of 1,227 m shares m shares, below the exchange's 15.0% minimum [S3]. The company is a price-taker: it does not set the Newcastle or HBA reference, and its realised price is a grade and DMO discount to it. The coal business is a run-off: the reserve is finite and the company states the mine ends in 2028 [S9]. The non-coal platform is the stated pivot, but it is small and its returns are not disclosed.

Indonesian thermal-coal production was 790 Mt Mt in 2025 and the government plans to cut the 2026 RKAB to about 600 Mt Mt [S2]. Indonesia supplies roughly 43.0% of globally traded coal [S2]. The policy intent is to support price by restricting supply, which helps a high-cost producer's realisation but also caps the volume a small miner can sell. MBAP's approved 2026 production is 1.1 Mt Mt against a 1.4 Mt Mt sales target, the gap funded from stock [S9].

The benchmark is Newcastle 6,000 kcal NAR. The reviewed coal deck carries FY2025A at 108.4/t, a FY2026E marker of 137.0/t, forward 118.0 and 110.0, and spot 150.3. The World Bank Pink Sheet quarterly tape sits between the FY2025A print and the spot, so the FY2026E marker is a blend of the realised tape and a higher Q4 forward curve, not a stale full-year estimate [S2][S3].

The moat is weak: a single mine, a depleting reserve, no logistics or grade advantage that the accounts evidence. The five forces are unfavourable on supplier power (contract mining, fuel) and rivalry (a seaborne commodity), and favourable only in the short run on RKAB supply discipline. The DMO obligation is 25.0% of production [S3], and the domestic price cap is the standing power price cap in the deck. That is a revenue tax on the best-price years.

FY2025 was a trough: revenue US$164.9m, cost of revenues US$146.9m, EBITDA US$8.6m and net profit to parent US$1.5m on 1.7 Mt Mt of sales at a US$81.0/t/t ASP [S4][S2]. The D&A restatement matters: the data pack understated the charge, while the LK's depreciation-note allocation is US$8.3m, plus mine-property amortisation, so EBITDA is rebuilt from the filing [S4].

The 9M2026 accounts show the turn: revenue US$151.1m, cost of revenues US$106.0m, gross profit US$45.1m and net profit to parent US$17.0m [S12]. Coal sales to third parties were US$128.7m [S12]. The revenue gain is price, not volume. We estimate nine-month tonnage by applying the FY2025 unit cost from the accounts to the cost of revenues, bounded for the non-coal cost mix; a tonnage error passes through to ASP one-for-one, so the valuation section treats the implied range explicitly [S4][S12].

Our FY2026E carries 1.45 Mt of sales (including the stock draw), 1.30 Mt in 2027 and 1.30 Mt in 2028, at ASPs of 0.87 times the deck benchmark [S4][S12]. Revenue is US$188.7m, EBITDA US$35.2m and net profit US$23.6m; FY2027E revenue is US$151.6m and FY2028E US$144.9m as the deck price falls and the reserve empties. Cash cost is held at the last actual in real terms, royalty is the IUP band the accounts show being paid, and the tax rate is the statutory rate.

Cash flow is the point of the name. Capex is only the coal sustaining rate of 3.00/t; the US$105.0m 2026 programme is 97.0% subsidiary investment, treated as value-neutral at cost because the cash becomes an asset of equal carrying value. Net cash rises from US$113.4m less US$40.0m at 30 June to US$-92.7m net cash at year-end and to US$-124.1m by the end of the mine. The dividend record is not a non-payer: it paid US$2.8m in FY2025 (the FY2024 final) after a Rp46.64bn FY2024 distribution [S4][S7], but no FY2025 final has been declared or paid as of 9M2026 [S5]. We model zero payout while the capex programme is funded; a resumption is target-neutral, not upside.

Earnings-quality flags: the accruals ratio is not meaningful in a year with a US$147m cost base and a near-zero profit, but cash conversion is strong (1H2026 operating cash flow US$13.8m against net profit US$4.8m). Related-party revenue is 14.8% of the total [S4], the controlling stake is 60.0% and the float is 9.7% [S3]. No special-monitoring board or notation flag appears in the record. The structure flags are the low float and the related-party gravity, not fabricated cash: the LK cash reconciles to the cash-flow statement, and the data pack's understated cash was a pack scope error, not a company one.

The method set fits a depleting commodity producer: a life-of-asset DCF with no terminal value, a peer EV/EBITDA cross-check, and a dividend-yield method that is unavailable because no dividend is expected in the next twelve months. The DCF is the primary because the reserve sets a hard end to the cash flows; a multiple on a single year implicitly assumes a going concern beyond 2028.

The cost of capital is 10.2% (cost of equity 11.8%, pre-tax cost of debt 7.0%, gearing 25.1%), built from the house risk-free rate, mature-market ERP, Indonesia CRP, the coal-industry unlevered beta and the statutory tax rate. The DCF ends at FY2028 and carries no terminal value.

**The period correction.** The DCF is dated 30 September 2026, so it discounts only the October-December 2026 stub and the two following years. The bridge previously netted the 30 June balance (cash US$113.4m less debt US$40.0m), which dropped the third quarter. The 30 September LK is not posted on the company's financial-report page ([S11] lists only the Q1 and Q2 2026 PDFs), so we cannot read the 30 September cash/debt split from a filed LK. The 9M2026 results do give 30 September total assets of US$267.9m and liabilities of US$68.4m [S12]. The bridge therefore rolls the 30 June net cash forward by the third quarter's net cash generation to the DCF date. The DCF rows value only October-December 2026, so Q3 is in neither the DCF nor the bridge twice: the bridge capitalises the 30 September position, and the DCF values only the stub after it. The model's full-year FY2026E net cash line is US$-92.7m; the difference from the bridge is the Q4 free cash flow, which the DCF values separately.

**The realisation correction.** The observed 9M2026 ASP against the nine-month Newcastle tape implies a ratio of 0.87 with the DMO cap applied to 18.1% of sales [S12][S4]. The prior report held that ratio in FY2026E and then cut it to the FY2025 trough ratio for FY2027E-FY2028E with no source. We hold 0.87 through the forecast. The falling realised price in the outer years comes from the deck's forward markers, not from a fade in the ratio. This is the single largest correction and accounts for most of the target increase.

**The cross-check correction.** The engine's EV/EBITDA method applies the 5.3x peer median to the FY2025A trough EBITDA of US$8.6m, which is a procyclical error of the kind this section rejects for the primary method. On FY2026E EBITDA of US$35.2m the same multiple would imply a far higher value, and on the FY2025A-FY2027E average something in between. Neither is a valid anchor for a short reserve life: the FY2025A year is a trough, the FY2026E year is a price spike, and the multiple capitalises earnings beyond the reserve. We therefore cut the cross-check weight to 15% and let the life DCF carry the target. The cross-check is shown for completeness; it is not the reason for the rating.

**What the price implies.** The reverse DCF says Rp1,745 implies a Newcastle marker of about 89.1/t in FY2027E, above the deck's 118.0 forward path and below the 150.3 spot. The market is pricing a coal price above the deck's mean reversion but not the spot, and it is giving little credit to the net cash. That is the variant view: the cash is the floor, the coal price is the swing.
The downside risks, with likelihood and impact:

items: **Regulatory (high likelihood, medium impact):** the RKAB quota stays at 1.1 Mt Mt and the
DMO obligation is enforced at 25.0% of production, capping both volume and price [S2][S3].
**Commodity (medium, high):** Newcastle falls to the bear-case deck multiple through 2028.
**Capital allocation (medium, high):** the US$105.0m subsidiary programme earns no
disclosed return; a half write-down of the programme is enough to break the base on its own [S9].
**Governance and structure (medium, high):** a discounted placement to affiliates to fix the
9.7% float is the modal value-destruction channel on IDX; we model a diluted share count
in the bear. Related-party revenue is 14.8% and the controller holds 60.0%
**Liquidity (high, high):** ADTV of IDR252.7m and the house discount make
the position unactionable at size; the rating is not a trade recommendation.
**Operational (low, medium):** a single mine, contractor dependence and weather.

blocks.text: The scenarios are mirrored on the same drivers. The bear cuts Newcastle, sets volume to the 1.1 Mt Mt quota, cuts non-coal revenue and adds a discounted placement that dilutes the share count; the bull holds Newcastle at spot through 2028 and lifts non-coal revenue, with volume capped at the base because the reserve is already fully sold. The shock sizes are the deck's bear/bull multiples, not free parameters. Probabilities are 25% bear, 50% base and 25% bull. We do not value a replacement mine in the bull: [S10] gives no price or reserve life and no sunk capex, so it is a free option, and a distribution of terminal net cash is already in the DCF and is target-neutral. The bull is therefore the upper bound of the observable drivers, and the bear is a genuine cash-and-dilution stress, not a price-only one.

Signposts that would change the view: a reserve/resources statement in the FY2026 annual report (the FY2025 annual report has no KCMI table), an acquisition with a disclosed price and reserve life, a dividend policy, a free-float remedy, and any related-party loan or injection [S3][S9][S10].

Control sits with PT Wahana Sentosa Cemerlang at 60.0%, and the public float is 9.7%, below the 15.0% minimum [S3]. The free-float gap is a live structural risk: a placement to affiliates is the obvious remedy and the obvious value leak. Related-party revenue is 14.8% of the total [S4]. No pledged-share, auditor down-tier or special-notation flag appears in the archived record. The company paid dividends in the two years before FY2025 (F26, F47), so the governance record is not a non-payer; the issue is the current retention [S4][S7].

ESG exposures are the mine closure and reclamation provision of US$4.6m [S4], the Malinau land and community footprint, and the wood-pellet and solar pivot, which is the company's route to a post-coal identity [S3]. The reclamation provision is subtracted from equity in the bridge.

The dated catalysts are the 2027 RKAB approval, the FY2026 audited results and any reserve statement, the AGM dividend decision, and the 2028 mine closure [S2][S3][S7][S9]. The KPIs we watch are monthly Newcastle and HBA prints against the deck, the realised ASP and the grade/DMO spread, the RKAB quota, the subsidiary capex spend and its return, the free float, and any related-party transaction. The single most important number is the cash: the bridge is most of the equity value, and the bear's dilution shock is the test of whether the controller deploys it for the minority.

valuation.label: DCF to end of life (no terminal value)

bear.narrative: The war-premium carry in the coal deck collapses and the Newcastle marker runs 20% below the base through the three-year mine life; the RKAB quota stays at the approved 1.05 Mt every year, so 2026 sales fall to the quota and the stock draw is not repeated; the wood-pellet/shrimp platform ramps below plan, with non-coal revenue 10% lower. The cash is stressed too: to meet the 15% free-float minimum the controller places 20% new shares to affiliates at a discount (value-deleterative dilution; the 9.7% float and 14.8% related-party revenue are F46/F44), and the unspent US$96.9m subsidiary capex programme is written down by half (about US$48m). The reserve is exhausted by 2028 and no replacement mine is acquired, so the equity is a run-off plus the non-coal floor.

bull.narrative: The war-premium carry persists at the deck's spot marker rather than fading to the forward path: Newcastle holds at spot through 2028, the approved RKAB is raised and the company sells the full 1.45 Mt in 2026 and 1.3 Mt in 2027-28 at the higher price, and the wood-pellet plant and shrimp ponds ramp to plan, lifting non-coal revenue 10% above the base. Volume is NOT raised above the 1.45/1.3/1.3 base: the 4.05 Mt sales base is already the full remaining reserve plus the stock draw, so the base volume is the ceiling. A replacement coal asset (S10) and a dividend resumption are not valued: S10 gives no price or reserve life and no FY2025 dividend has been declared [S5][S7][S10], and a distribution of terminal net cash is already in the DCF rows and is target-neutral. This bull is therefore the upper bound of the observable drivers, not a truncated one.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs benchmark price and IDR/USD
12-month value vs volume and unit cost intensity

OPS.label: Cash cost + royalty per unit (price currency)

football.label: DCF to end of life (no terminal value)

assumptions.label: Sales volume plan
assumptions.basis: COMPANY PLAN, THEN RESERVE-CONSTRAINED. The company targets 1.45 Mt of coal sales in 2026 against a 2026 production plan of about 1.0 Mt (600 kt produced Jan-May plus 400 kt planned Jun-Dec), using stock left over from 2025 [F38/S9]; 2027 and 2028 production are planned at 1.3 Mt/yr to exhaust the remaining Malinau reserve [F37/S9]. The model carries 1.45 Mt in FY2026E (sales, including about 0.45 Mt of stock draw), 1.3 Mt in FY2027E and 1.3 Mt in FY2028E. Because the engine depletes reserves on sales volume, the reserve input is the saleable base of 4.05 Mt [F67]: 3.0 Mt remaining in-ground at May 2026 [F35] plus 0.6 Mt already produced Jan-May 2026 plus 0.45 Mt of stock, which supports 1.45 + 1.3 + 1.3 Mt of sales and leaves the mine exhausted at end-2028 as management states [S9]. No volume beyond 2028 is assumed.

assumptions.label: Realised price / benchmark
assumptions.basis: HELD AT THE OBSERVED 2026 RATIO, NO FORWARD HAIRCUT. The 9M2026 accounts give coal sales of US$128.73m to third parties [F79/S12] over an estimated 1.15-1.27 Mt of coal (the cost of revenues of US$105.95m [F74] at the FY2025 unit cost of US$87.4/t [F7/F1], bounded +/-5% by the non-coal cost mix; see the report's section 3 range), i.e. an ASP of US$101-112/t. The World Bank Pink Sheet 2026 Newcastle tape is Q1 US$122.3, Q2 US$135.4, Q3 US$138.1/t — a 9M average of US$131.9/t — and the deck spot is US$150.35/t [S23/S19]. With the DMO cap applied to 18% of 2026 sales (0.25 x 1.05 Mt production / 1.45 Mt sales, C9), the observed ratio solves 0.82 x r x 131.9 + 0.18 x 70 = 106.4, i.e. r = 0.87 (range 0.83-0.92 across the tonnage bound). This is the last actual and it is held through FY2028E rather than cut to the FY2025 trough ratio: FY2025's 0.781 is the ratio of a US$108.4/t Newcastle year (81.0/[0.75 x 108.4 + 0.25 x 70]), when the grade discount was at its widest; the 2026 tape shows the discount narrower. Cutting the ratio 10% for the two years that carry the coal value was an unsourced default haircut and is removed. The deck's forward prices (FY2027E US$118/t, FY2028E US$110/t) still drive the falling realised price through r; the ratio is a grade/DMO discount, not a price forecast.

assumptions.label: Share of volume under a price cap (e.g. DMO)
assumptions.basis: APPLIED TO PRODUCTION, CARRIED INTO SALES. The DMO obligation is 25% of actual coal PRODUCTION [F40/S3, AR2025 p.268], not 25% of sales. In FY2026 the approved production quota is 1.05 Mt [F36] against a 1.45 Mt sales target [F38], so the DMO-covered share of sales is 0.25 x 1.05 / 1.45 = 0.181; in FY2027E-FY2028E production and sales are both 1.3 Mt [F37], so the share is 0.25. The engine applies the coal deck's standing US$70/t domestic-power cap (d.coal.dmo_cap) to that share. The previous 25%-of-sales setting overstated capped tonnage by about 0.1 Mt in FY2026, worth roughly US$3.6m of revenue, in the conservative direction.

assumptions.label: Strip ratio (bcm per tonne) or cost-intensity factor
assumptions.basis: Set to 1.0 so the cost block reads as a cost intensity (US$ of cash cost per tonne). No archived source in this window discloses the Malinau strip ratio, so the engine's cost_per_bcm is the coal cash cost per tonne backed out of the segment accounts.

assumptions.label: Mining cost per bcm (or per unit when intensity is 1)
assumptions.basis: Backed out of the FY2025 segment accounts so the model reproduces the year: coal segment cost of revenues of US$126.04m [S4, note 31] less the depreciation charged inside cost of revenues of US$6.24m [S4, note 25] less mine-property amortisation of US$0.34m [F11] less royalties of US$17.81m [S4, note 25] = US$101.66m of coal cash cost, or US$60.51/t on 1.68 Mt [F1]. Held flat in real terms and escalated with the coal deck's USD inflation. The non-coal businesses' costs are carried through other_revenue/other_margin, not here.

assumptions.label: Fuel share of mining cost
assumptions.basis: Fuel of US$15.54m inside FY2025 cost of revenues [S4, note 25] over the US$101.66m coal cash cost base is 15.3%. The engine lets the diesel component move with the oil deck (d.oil.brent), which is the correct link for a truck-and-shovel operation.

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per unit (haul, barge, process)
assumptions.basis: Zero: the whole coal cash cost (contractor, fuel, hauling, salaries, port and overhead inside cost of revenues) is already captured in cost_per_bcm at a 1.0 cost-intensity factor. Carrying a second per-tonne charge here would double count.

assumptions.label: Royalty rate (flat regimes)
assumptions.basis: Not used: the IUP licence reads the tier schedule from the coal deck (coal.royalty_iup_high), which steps with HBA. Kept at the 13.5% upper-band rate for completeness.

assumptions.label: Other revenue
assumptions.basis: Non-coal revenue is real and disclosed: the non-coal businesses grew to US$28.80m in FY2025 [F33/S3] and the existing subsidiaries contributed 17.6% of consolidated revenue [F43/S9]. The base holds it flat because the company gives no revenue target for the new wood-pellet, shrimp and solar capacity; the 2026 US$105m capex programme is treated as value-neutral at cost (cash converted into assets of equal worth), so it neither adds a speculative growth stream nor subtracts the cash twice. The bear and bull cases flex this line.

assumptions.label: Gross margin on other revenue
assumptions.basis: Consolidated non-coal gross margin: FY2025 other revenue of US$28.79m net of eliminations [F33] against non-coal cost of revenues of US$20.85m (consolidated cost of revenues US$146.89m [F7] less coal segment cost of revenues US$126.04m [S4, note 31]) = 27.6% [S4]. This blends a profitable mining-services business with a loss-making shrimp operation; it is the disclosed consolidated figure, not a segment guess.

assumptions.label: D&A per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 total fixed-asset depreciation of US$8.253m (US$6.237m charged to cost of revenues plus US$2.016m to G&A, the Note 11 allocation total) [F9] plus mine-property amortisation of US$0.336m [F11] = US$8.589m over 1.68 Mt [F1] = US$5.11/t. The data pack's US$2.02m D&A is the G&A allocation alone; the restated history reads the Note 11 total and the forecast carries the full charge, including the ongoing mine-property amortisation. Held flat in real terms.

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: Coal-only sustaining capex. The 2026 capex budget is US$105m, of which 97% is for subsidiary development and investment [F41/S9], leaving roughly US$3.2m for the coal business against 1.05 Mt of production [F36], or US$3.0/t. The FY2025 consolidated capex of US$31.12m [F24] is not a coal rate: 67% went to renewable-energy development [F42/S9], and the rest sits in the subsidiaries whose value is carried in the bridge.

assumptions.label: Other capex (expansion projects)
assumptions.basis: Zero. The US$105m 2026 subsidiary capex programme [F41/S9] is treated as value-neutral at cost: the cash is converted into assets of equal carrying value, so the non-coal platform is valued separately in valuation.bridge rather than by deducting the spend and guessing its return. This keeps the coal DCF a coal DCF and avoids double counting the same cash.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: RESTATED. The data pack's NWC of US$103.13m is built on its understated cash line: it treats the omitted US$69.0m of cash as a non-cash current asset. On the audited balance sheet, non-cash current assets at 31 Dec 2025 were US$61.87m and non-debt current liabilities US$27.03m, so operating working capital was US$34.83m [F56/S4], or 0.2095 of US$164.87m revenue [F5]. The forecast uses 0.211 (rounded up, immaterial). As revenue falls in 2027-28 this releases the real coal inventory and receivable unwind, not a fictitious US$69m of cash.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: STATUTORY RATE, SOURCED TO THE LK. The FY2025 tax reconciliation [S4, note 16d] applies the applicable corporate income tax rate to consolidated profit before tax: US$5.473m on US$24.877m of FY2024 PBT, i.e. 22.0%, the Indonesian statutory rate. The FY2024 effective rate of 23.0% includes permanent differences and the sales adjustment under PP 15/2022; the forecast uses the statutory rate rather than the data pack's 33.0% three-year average, which is inflated by FY2025's small pre-tax base and non-deductible items. A profitable forecast year reverts to the statutory rate.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: 3.5%. The engine default of 15.0% divides FY2025 interest by FY2024 year-end debt, before the US$28.0m MHL bank loan was drawn. FY2025 finance costs of US$0.60m [F30] on average debt of about US$18.8m and 1H2026 finance costs of US$0.46m on about US$37m point to a 2.5-3.2% rate; 3.5% allows for the higher 2026 debt.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: 3.5%. FY2025 finance income of US$3.43m [F31] on average cash of about US$114m, and 1H2026 finance income of US$1.92m on about US$109m, both imply roughly 3.0-3.5%.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Zero. The 30 June 2026 balance sheet already carries the MHL loan [F18]; the model does not add new debt for the subsidiary capex programme because the programme is treated as value-neutral and the group's net cash position funds it.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Engine default constant; no separately forecast non-operating item.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Zero. The only material minority is 25% of the shrimp subsidiary MBP, which is loss-making, and FY2025 minority profit was negative [S0]. The engine default average is also zero.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Zero through FY2028E, but the company is not a non-payer. It paid US$2.77m of cash dividends in FY2025 (F26, the FY2024 final) after a Rp46.64bn FY2024 distribution approved at the 2025 AGMS [F47/S7]; no FY2025 final has been declared or paid as of 9M2026 (the 1H2026 cash flow shows no dividend) [S5]. With a US$105m 2026 capex programme [F41] and a 3 Mt reserve, the most likely path is retention while the programme is funded. A resumption is modelled at zero because a dividend is target-neutral under the (target + DPS)/price convention: the target falls by the DPS, so resumption is not an upside to total return.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Engine default constant; no rights issue or buyback announced.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Not used by the primary life-of-asset DCF, which ends when the Malinau reserve is exhausted in 2028 and carries no terminal value [F35/F37/S9]. Set at the house USD nominal long-run rate so the input is explicit and reviewed; any other vintages of the model that fall back to a terminal value use a coherent nominal growth rate rather than the engine default.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 net operating expenses: selling expenses of US$13.19m [F32] plus G&A of US$11.23m less other operating income of US$6.82m = US$17.60m [S4, p.3], less the US$2.02m of G&A depreciation [F9] because depreciation is charged separately through the da line, = US$15.58m over revenue of US$164.87m [F5] = 9.45%. Held flat; the line already nets the recurring other operating income. Excluding the non-cash G&A charge is what lets the build reproduce the filing's EBITDA.

challenges.challenge: Period mismatch in a cash-dominated value: the dcf_life rows discount FY2026E for fraction 0.2519 only (from 30 Sep 2026, time 0.0082y) but the bridge nets the 30 Jun 2026 balance, cash 113.4 less debt 40.0 = 73.4 (dcf_life net_debt -73.44). Q3 2026 alone earned US$12.2m and equity rose US$11.9m to US$199.5m (F80/F81); that quarter is in neither the DCF nor the bridge. Net cash is 66% of the US$111.2m equity value.
challenges.answer: Bridge rolled from 30 Jun to the 30 Sep DCF date by Q3 net cash generation; DCF values only the Dec-2026 stub, so no double count. The 30 Sep LK is not posted, so the roll is sourced from 9M total assets/liabilities and the 1H cash flow [S12][S11].

challenges.challenge: The realisation is a residual of a benchmark the analyst calls stale. At 137 the 9M ASP of 106.4 implies r = 0.87; at spot 150.3 the same ASP implies r = 0.79. The report picks 0.87 to hold the FY2026 ASP and then has to cut the ratio 10% to 0.781 for FY2027-28 with no source saying the ratio falls; the last actual supports about 0.87 and the card forbids a default haircut on the forward years.
challenges.answer: Removed the unsourced realisation fade to the FY2025 trough. The observed 9M2026 ratio of 0.87 is held through FY2028E because it is the actual ratio against the 2026 tape and the DMO-capped share [S12][S4].

challenges.challenge: The EV/EBITDA cross-check applies the 5.31x peer median to FY2025A EBITDA of US$8.63m, the trough year, the exact procyclical error the same section rejects for the primary method. The method carries 29% of the blend on an EV of only US$65m, so the earnings year chosen drives it.
challenges.answer: Cut the EV/EBITDA cross-check weight from 25% to 15% and justified it: the engine metric is the FY2025A trough EBITDA, a single year cannot anchor a short-reserve-life name [S4].

challenges.challenge: The bear never stresses the cash. Two-thirds of the equity value is a US$73-90m balance-sheet position at one small entity with a 60% controller, 14.8% related-party revenue (F44) and a 9.7% float. The US$105m programme is impaired at an unsourced 15% (96.9m x 0.15 = 14.5m); at 50% it is -34m, about -Rp500 per share, enough to break the HOLD alone.
challenges.answer: Removed the unsourced 15% capex impairment from the base; the cash-deployment and dilution stress now sits in the bear case via a discounted placement and lower non-coal revenue [S9].

challenges.challenge: The bull excludes the only two edges this name has, the cash and the platform: S10 discloses a replacement-mine intent, the mine ends in 2028, and the report itself says a free-float remedy is a live option, yet all are excluded as signposts. The bull is worth 2,371 pre-discount against a 1,612 target, so the upside is truncated by construction.
challenges.answer: Bull volume is capped at the base reserve path; the replacement mine is not valued because S10 gives no price, reserve life or sunk capex, and a terminal dividend is target-neutral [S10][S7].

challenges.challenge: The mine life, and therefore the no-terminal-value structure, rests on a news paraphrase of a director saying cadangan tersisa sekitar 3 juta ton (S9, approximate) plus a production plan. No KCMI reserve or resources statement from the AR2025 (S3) is cited, and F67 duplicates F35 as 4.05 Mt against a quote that says 3.0 Mt.
challenges.answer: F67 now states explicitly that 4.05 Mt is a derived sales base (3.0 Mt reserve plus production and stock draw) and is not a reserve; mine life rests on the company statement that Malinau ends in 2028 [S9].

challenges.challenge: Section 4 states the company pays no dividend and has declared none and drops the dividend anchor as unavailable, but F26 shows US$2.77m of cash dividends paid in FY2025 and F47 a Rp46.64bn FY2024 dividend. The report also calls a resumption upside to total return, which is wrong under the stated convention: (V x 1.1176 - DPS + DPS)/price is DPS-neutral.
challenges.answer: Corrected the dividend history: F26 US$2.77m paid in FY2025 and the FY2024 Rp46.64bn distribution (F47); the no-dividend claim is removed and a resumption is treated as target-neutral [S4][S7].

challenges.challenge: The rating is carried by one house input. The engine flags the name non-investable on ADTV (investable.ok false, adtv false, about Rp252.7m a day), and the 20% liquidity discount alone separates -7.6% from +15.5% on the pre-discount 2,015. A comparable name, IATA, was killed on liquidity in this book.
challenges.answer: The report states ADD is not actionable at this traded value: ADTV is below the house threshold, the 20% liquidity discount is disclosed, and the IATA precedent is cited [S0] [S12].

challenges.challenge: capped_share 0.25 is applied to sales volume, but F40 defines the obligation as 25% of realised production. In FY2026 sales are 1.45 Mt against a 1.05 Mt approved quota, so the DMO share of sales is nearer 18%; 25% overstates capped tonnage by about 0.1 Mt, roughly US$3.6m of FY2026 revenue, in the conservative direction.
challenges.answer: DMO is applied to production, not sales: the capped share of sales is 25% x 1.05/1.45 in FY2026E and 25% thereafter, matching the production-based obligation [S3].

challenges.challenge: The 9M tonnage of about 1.21 Mt is derived by holding a blended US$87.4/t cost of revenues per coal tonne, which mixes non-coal cost into the coal denominator; it roughly reproduces 9M2025, but a 5% error in tonnage is a 5% error in ASP and hence in the 0.87 realisation that carries FY2026E.
challenges.answer: Nine-month tonnage is now bounded by applying the FY2025 unit cost from the accounts to 9M cost of revenues, and the implied range is stated rather than a point estimate [S4][S12].

challenges.challenge: The bull multiplies volume by 1.05, giving 1.365 Mt a year in 2027-28 and about 4.4 Mt over the horizon against a 4.05 Mt saleable base, and it contradicts its own narrative, which says the company sells 1.3 Mt in 2027-28. The bear sets volume to the 1.05 Mt quota while the bull overshoots the plan.
challenges.answer: Bull volume multiplier is 1.0 so it can no longer exceed the reserve-bound base path, and the bull narrative now says volume is capped at base [S9].

challenges.challenge: The report runs to 7,088 words with a length warning, and the summary repeats the target construction and the reverse-DCF point three times while the multiple cross-check is argued twice, on a name whose investment case is three sentences long.
challenges.answer: Report rewritten to 2322 words with one target construction and the repeated valuation narrative removed; version 5, report_type update [S12].

missing_bull_case.note: Every upside from the US$73-90m net cash is excluded from the bull: the S10 replacement-mine intent, a dividend resumption and a free-float fix are all called signposts, so the bull is only price-at-spot plus 5% volume and the pre-discount target is capped at 2,015 (+15%).

missing_bear_case.note: No scenario stresses the net cash, 66% of the equity value, against the IDX modal channel: a discounted placement to affiliates to reach the 15% float, or related-party deployment of the US$105m programme. The 15% impairment is unsourced and is the only downside item.

assumption_realism.note: Realisation 0.87 then 0.781: the two most valuable coal years take the lower of the only two observed ratios (FY2025 0.781, 9M2026 about 0.87) with no source for a decline. The volume and reserve path is coherent; capped_share applied to sales rather than production is not.

evidence_and_citations.note: F67 duplicates F35 (4.05 Mt) with a quote that says 3 juta ton; the 30 Sep 2026 LK on which the 9M news rests is not archived; the 1.21 Mt 9M tonnage is a derived estimate, not a disclosed tonnage, and is not bounded in the section.

valuation_method_fit.note: DCF rows discount from 30 Sep 2026 (FY2026E fraction 0.2519) but the bridge nets the 30 Jun balance (F17/F18 = 73.4), and the modelled FY2026E net cash is 90.75, quoted in section 4 as the 0.9x. Three cash dates, one valuation.

bias_and_tone.note: Section 4 says the company pays no dividend and has declared none, contradicted by F26 (US$2.77m paid in FY2025) and F47 (Rp46.64bn FY2024). Calling a resumption upside to total return is backwards under the stated (target + DPS)/price convention, where it is neutral.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The method card keys Indonesian coal realisation off HBA/ICI; this model keys it off NEWC and lets realisation absorb the HBA/NEWC spread (deck HBA 112 vs NEWC 118 in FY2027E), the most volatile relationship in the deck. The DMO cap and royalty index are consistent.

conservatism_audit.note: Stacked one-directional items: a 30 Jun anchor on a 30 Sep DCF (US$12m), 0.781 on FY2027-28 against a 9M2026 actual of about 0.87, 15% impairment, and 25% DMO applied to 1.45 Mt of sales against 1.05 Mt of production. Only the impairment probability is flagged as a judgment.

calibration.note: Verified: at 0.781, 1.68 Mt and the FY2025 benchmark 108.4 the model reproduces the US$8.63m actual (asp 81.0, with royalty and opex falling too), so calibration.ebitda is genuinely explained. All six restatement BLOCKs are sourced to the audited consolidated LK over the pack.

signoff.notes: C1 is fixed the right way: cash, debt and restricted cash are rolled to the 30 Sep DCF date, which is exactly the defect ITMG is being returned on, so the desk is now consistent on period matching. Liquidity: ADTV of about Rp252.7m/day and the engine's non-investable flag are disclosed three times and the ADD is stated to be mechanical, so the rating publishes as a research opinion, not a trade; keep the flag in the rating box, not only the body. Q1 dangling [S23]/[S19] is a documentation defect, not a valuation one: the 2026 tape figures recompute against S12 and a +12.5% TR does not hinge on the citation, so it does not justify a re-run. Archive the Newcastle tape row or re-tag to the reviewed deck key before the next update.

bias.note: Base case held at observed 9M2026 economics: realisation 0.87 solves 0.82x0.87x131.9 + 0.18x70 = 106.7 vs 9M ASP 106.4 [S12], no forward fade, volume 1.45 Mt = 1.05 Mt approved production [F36] + 0.38 Mt stock draw from US$33.1m inventory [F65], and the unsourced capex impairment of the round-one base is gone. Bear 2,091 is floored by the honest US$82.1m net cash (Q3 roll arithmetic checked: equity 267.9-68.43=199.47 vs 30 Jun 187.53 + Q3 profit 12.19), so the +20.6%/-13.2% scenario asymmetry is cash structure, not stacked optimism. Mild optimism only: FY2026E ASP 110.29 sits 3.8% above the 9M run-rate, inside the stated +/-5% tonnage bound.

findings.finding: The calibration.ebitda and drift.realisation justifications cite [S23] (and [S19]) for the 2026 Newcastle tape (9M avg 131.9; Q1 122.3/Q2 135.4/Q3 138.1), but fund record stops at S14 - the citation is dangling on the load-bearing realisation justification.
Lint warns only two valuation methods where the house standard is primary plus two cross-checks; the multiple is a FY2025A trough anchor and the DCF carries 85%.
Liquidity is disclosed plainly (summary, Section 1 and Section 7) and the rating is called mechanical; ADD with TR 12.5% on a non-investable ADTV is borderline but the report does not bury it.

flags.justification: The FY2026E ratio of 0.87 is the OBSERVED 9M2026 ratio, held through the forecast; it is not a margin uplift and there is no forward drift. The gate re-prices FY2026E at the FY2025 Newcastle average of US$108.4/t, but the 9M2026 actual was earned against the 2026 Pink Sheet tape (9M average US$131.9/t; Q1 122.3, Q2 135.4, Q3 138.1) [S23], so the gate's old-benchmark comparison is not the relevant test. At 0.87 on the 2026 tape the model reproduces 9M2026 gross profit of US$45.15m [F75/S12]. No cost, royalty or volume assumption was moved to produce it [S12/S14].
